hints: Focus on electrons first, a redox equation only works when electrons lost equal electrons gained.
The oxidation half-equation gives $2e^-$ but the reduction needs $6e^-$, so multiply the whole oxidation equation by 3.
Add the two halves together, then cancel the $6H^+$ made by oxidation against the $14H^+$ used in reduction to find what is left.
walkthrough:
**Balance the electrons**

The key idea is simple. What is lost must be gained. Oxidation releases electrons, reduction takes them up.

Oxidation: $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O} + 2\text{H}^+ + 2e^-$

Reduction: $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^+ + 6e^- \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$

To get $6e^-$ on both sides, multiply oxidation by 3:
$$3\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} \rightarrow 3\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O} + 6\text{H}^+ + 6e^-$$

**Add the halves and cancel**

Now add everything together, reactants with reactants and products with products.
$$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^+ + 3\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O} + 3\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O} + 6\text{H}^+$$
Cancel $6\text{H}^+$ from both sides ($14 - 6 = 8$ left on the left):
$$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 8\text{H}^+ + 3\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O} + 3\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$$

**Check atoms and charge**

A quick check builds confidence. Left has 2 Cr, 7 O from dichromate plus 3 O from ethanol, and 8 + 18 = 26 H. Right has 7 O from water plus 3 O from ethanal, and 14 + 12 = 26 H. Charge left is $-2 + 8 = +6$, right is $2 \times (+3) = +6$. It all balances.

options.A: Correct. This uses 3 ethanols to supply the 6 electrons needed by one dichromate, and correctly cancels $H^+$ to leave $8H^+$ on the left and $7H_2O$ on the right. Atoms and charge both balance.
options.B: Incorrect. This uses only 1 ethanol, so only $2e^-$ are supplied but $6e^-$ are needed. Electrons do not balance, a common trap if you forget to multiply the oxidation half-equation.
options.C: Incorrect. Although 3 ethanols are used, the $H^+$ and $H_2O$ are wrong. This comes from cancelling water or $H^+$ incorrectly instead of doing $14H^+ - 6H^+ = 8H^+$ and keeping $7H_2O$.
options.D: Incorrect. This adds the halves without cancelling the $6H^+$ produced by oxidation. You cannot just keep $14H^+$ on the left, you must subtract the $H^+$ that appear on the right.
